origin.description: Writes a data frame to an SPSS .sav file.
origin.usage: write_sav(data, path, compress = c("byte", "none", "zsav"), adjust_tz = TRUE)

arguments.name: compress
arguments.text: "byte", "none", or "zsav". TRUE means zsav and FALSE means none.

arguments.name: adjust_tz
arguments.text: When true, a zoned datetime is written as the same clock time in UTC.

origin.details: Names must be valid SPSS names. User-missing values and ranges on a labelled_spss column are written. A factor level longer than 120 characters is rejected.
origin.example:
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".sav")
x <- labelled_spss(c(1, 9), c(Good = 1), na_values = 9, label = "q")
write_sav(tibble::tibble(q = x), tmp)
print(read_sav(tmp, user_na = TRUE))
unlink(tmp)

translation.description: Writes a data frame to an SPSS .sav file.

arguments.name: compress
arguments.text: "byte", "none", or "zsav". TRUE means zsav and FALSE means none.

arguments.name: adjust_tz
arguments.text: When true, a zoned datetime is written as the same clock time in UTC.

translation.details: Names must be valid SPSS names. User-missing values and ranges on a labelled_spss column are written. A factor level longer than 120 characters is rejected.
translation.example:
import os, tempfile
from haven import labelled_spss, read_sav, write_sav
from tibble import new_tibble
path = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".sav")
x = labelled_spss([1, 9], {"Good": 1}, na_values=[9], label="q")
write_sav(new_tibble([x], nrow=2, names=["q"]), path)
col = read_sav(path, user_na=True).columns[0]
print(col.values, col.na_values, col.label)
os.remove(path)
